[Al-Hamd lillah alladhi khalaqa al-samawat wa al-ard wa ja'ala al-zulumat wa al-nur] "Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light" — and created the night and the day. "Yet those who disbelieve" — after the proof of His oneness has been established by what was mentioned of His creation — "ascribe equals to their Lord" — they make stones and idols equal to Him, so they worship them along with Him. 0

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 2:

﴿He it is who created you from clay﴾ meaning: Adam, the father of mankind. ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ meaning: the term of life, from life until death. ﴿And a specified term is with Him﴾ meaning: from death until resurrection. ﴿Yet you⁠ — O polytheists⁠ — after this still ﴿doubt﴾, meaning: you have doubts and deny the resurrection. He intends: the One who initiated creation is able to bring it back.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 3:

﴿Wa-huwa Allah﴾ That is: the One worshipped, the Glorified, the One who alone manages (all affairs) ﴿in the heavens and in the earth﴾

﴿And no sign from the signs of their Lord comes to them﴾ indicating His oneness, such as what was mentioned of the creation of Adam and the creation of the night and the day, ﴿except that they turn away from it﴾, neglecting reflection upon it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 5:

﴿Then they have denied﴾ meaning: the polytheists of the people of Mecca. ﴿the truth when it came to them﴾ meaning: the Qur'an. ﴿So there will come to them the news of that which they used to mock﴾ i.e.: the reports of their mockery and its recompense.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 6:

﴿Did they not see﴾ meaning: these disbelievers ﴿how many generations We destroyed before them﴾, generations and nations ﴿We had established them on the earth as We have not established you﴾, We had given them more wealth, servants and livestock than We have given you ﴿and We sent down the sky﴾ rain ﴿upon them in abundance﴾, abundant in flow; (mudrar) is its coming and descending in great quantity ﴿then We destroyed them for their sins﴾, for their disbelief ﴿and We brought into being﴾ We created ﴿after them other generations﴾. This is an argument against those who deny the Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 7:

﴿And even if We had sent down to you a written scripture upon paper⌋ The polytheists of Makkah said: "We will not believe in you until you bring us a book from the heaven all at once, visible to us." So Allah said: ﴿And if We had sent down to you a scripture⌋ i.e., written, ﴿upon paper⌋ meaning: a page, ﴿and they had touched it with their hands⌋ so they witnessed that directly and touched it with their hands, ﴿those who disbelieved would surely say, "This is nothing but obvious magic."⌋ Allah the Exalted informed that they repel the proof; even if they saw the book descending from the heaven, they would say: "Magic."

"And they said, 'Why has an angel not been sent down to him?'" They asked for an angel whom they could see testifying to his prophethood. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided﴾, meaning they would have been destroyed by a total annihilating punishment, as was the practice with those before them who asked for signs and then did not believe. ﴿Then they would not be reprieved﴾, meaning they would not be given respite for repentance or for anything else.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 9:

﴿Had We made him an angel,﴾ that is, had We made the Messenger who descends to them, so that he might bear witness to his prophethood, an angel, as they demand, ﴿We would have made him a man.﴾ This is because they would not be able to see the angel in his true form, for the eyes of creation are bewildered when looking upon the angels. For this reason, Jibril, peace be upon him, used to come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the form of Dihyah al-Kalbi. ﴿And We would have confused them with what they confuse.﴾ That is, We would have mixed up for them what they mix up for themselves, so that they would be in doubt and not know whether he is an angel or a human being. In other words, what they sought was a state of confusion, not a state of clarification. Then Allah consoled His Prophet, peace be upon him, with His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 10:

﴿And certainly were the messengers before you mocked﴾, and they were denied and accused of sorcery. ﴿So there descended﴾, meaning it befell and came down, ﴿upon those who mocked﴾ the messengers ﴿that which they used to mock﴾, meaning the punishment, which they denied would ever occur.

Say, [O Muhammad], to them: ﴿Travel through the earth and then observe﴾ ‹ fa-i‘tabiru› (take admonition). ﴿How was the end of﴾ those who denied the messengers. That is: when they travel, they will see the traces of the bygone destroyed nations, as a warning to them of what befell those [nations].

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 12:

﴿Say, "To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?"﴾ If they answer you, [well]; otherwise, ﴿say, "To Allah belongs it. He has prescribed for Himself mercy."﴾ He obligated Himself to mercy, and this is a gentle invitation to turn back in repentance. ﴿He will surely gather you﴾ i.e., by Allah, He will surely gather you ﴿to the Day of Resurrection﴾, i.e., He will bring you together to this Day which you denied, and He will surely bring you and it together. Then he began, saying: ﴿Those who have lost themselves﴾ destroyed them through polytheism, ﴿they are the ones who will not believe.﴾

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿And to Him belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day.﴾

"That which dwells in them and that which they enclose": i.e., whatever resides in them and is contained by them, meaning: all created beings.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 14:

﴿Say, "Shall I take as a protector other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth?"﴾ The Creator of them both, initiating them from nothing. ﴿And He feeds but is not fed﴾ He provides sustenance and is not provided for.

"Whoever is spared from it on that day," ﴿من يصرف عنه﴾ — that is, the punishment — ﴿يومئذ﴾ (on that day, the Day of Resurrection), ﴿فقد رحمه﴾ — then indeed He has shown him mercy; that is, Allah has necessarily made mercy obligatory for him without doubt.
"And if Allah touches you with harm" — that is: if Allah makes the harm, which is sickness and poverty, touch you.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 18:

﴿And He is the Subduer﴾ (al-Qahir), the All-Powerful, whom nothing can overpower, ﴿over His servants﴾. That is: His dominion has risen over them, so they are under subjection.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 19:

﴿Say: "What thing is greatest in testimony?"﴾ The people of Makkah said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Bring us someone who testifies for you to prophethood, for the People of the Book deny you." So this verse was revealed. Allah the Exalted commanded Muhammad (peace be upon him) to ask them, then commanded him to inform them, saying: ﴿Allah is a witness between me and you﴾. That is: Allah, whom you have acknowledged as the Creator of the heavens and the earth, the darknesses and the light, testifies for me to prophethood by establishing proofs and sending down the Qur'an upon me. ﴿And this Qur'an has been revealed to me﴾, the Qur'an which is miraculous in its wording, its arrangement, and its reports of what has been and what will be, ﴿that I may warn you﴾, that I may frighten you, ﴿by it﴾, of the punishment of Allah for disbelief, ﴿and whomever it reaches﴾. That is: and whoever the Qur'an reaches after you. Everyone to whom the Qur'an reaches is as though he has seen Muhammad (peace be upon him). Say: ﴿Do you indeed testify that there are other gods with Allah?﴾ This is an interrogative whose meaning is denial and rejection. ﴿Say: "I do not testify"﴾, the verse...

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 20:

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book﴾ is explained in Surat al-Baqarah.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 21:

﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?﴾ Meaning: there is no one more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah, namely those whom He mentioned in His words: ﴿And when they commit an immoral act...﴾ (the verse) ﴿or denies His signs?﴾ That is, the Qur'an and Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.﴾ That is, whoever denies the lordship of his Lord and rejects His messengers will not be made happy. They are the ones who wronged themselves by destroying themselves with punishment.

And (remember) the Day when We will gather them all together, then We will say to those who associated partners (with Allah): "Where are your partners," i.e., your idols and your gods, "whom you used to claim" that they would intercede for you? This is a question of rebuke.

Then their fitna (trial/outcome) will not be except that: [the outcome of their being tempted by the idols and their love for them was only that] they disavowed them, so they said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 24:

﴿Look﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿how they lied against themselves﴾ by denying their polytheism in the Hereafter, ﴿and what they used to invent has vanished from them﴾, meaning: it departed and became void. ﴿What they used to invent﴾ refers to their worship of idols.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 25:

﴿And among them﴾ among the disbelievers, ﴿are those who listen to you﴾ when you recite the Qur'an, ﴿but We have placed over their hearts coverings﴾ veils, ﴿lest they understand it﴾ lest they comprehend it and fail to know the truth, ﴿and in their ears is deafness﴾ heaviness and deafness, so they hear nothing of it and gain no benefit from it. ﴿And if they see every sign﴾ every sign indicating your truthfulness, ﴿they will not believe in it﴾ this is their state of remoteness from faith. ﴿Until, when they come to you, disputing with you﴾ contending with you regarding the religion, ﴿those who disbelieve say﴾ whoever among them disbelieved says: ﴿This is not﴾ what this is ﴿except the legends of the former peoples﴾ the tales of earlier nations which they used to write down in their books.

﴿And they forbid [others] from it﴾, meaning they forbid people from following Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿and they keep far away from it﴾, meaning they distance themselves from him, so they do not believe in him. ﴿And they destroy none but themselves﴾, by persisting in disobedience to God, the Exalted; ﴿and they do not perceive it﴾, meaning they do not know that.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 27:

﴿And if you could see﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿when they are made to stand over the Fire﴾, i.e., they are held back over the Fire on the Sirat (the bridge over Hell), ﴿and they will say, "Oh, would that we could be returned!"﴾ They wish that they could be returned to the world so that they would believe. This is His saying: ﴿and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers.﴾ i.e., and we would not deny the signs of our Lord (after witnessing them directly), ﴿and be among the believers.﴾ They guaranteed that they would not deny and would believe. Then Allah the Exalted said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 28:

﴿Nay⁠—﴾ the matter is not as they wished in the return. ﴿What they used to conceal before has become apparent to them.﴾ That is, they had denied their polytheism, so God, glorified is He, made their limbs speak, and they testified against them with disbelief. The meaning: their disgrace became evident in the Hereafter, and their veils were torn away. ﴿And if they were returned, they would revert to what they were forbidden﴾ to, namely polytheism, because of the prior decree concerning them, that they were created for wretchedness. ﴿And indeed they are liars﴾ in their saying: ﴿And we would not deny the signs of our Lord.﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 29:

﴿And they said﴾ meaning: the disbelievers, ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world﴾ they denied the resurrection.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 30:

﴿And if you could see when they are made to stand before their Lord﴾ They will recognise their Lord out of necessity. It was also said: they will be made to stand over the questioning of their Lord and His rebuke of them. This is confirmed by His saying: ﴿Is this not the truth?﴾ That is, this resurrection? Then they will acknowledge it at a time when that acknowledgement will not benefit them, and they will say: ﴿Yes, by our Lord!﴾ Then God, exalted is He, will say: ﴿So taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve﴾ — because of your disbelief.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 31:

﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost,﴾ by the resurrection and the return to Allah. ﴿Until, when the Hour comes upon them suddenly,﴾ unexpectedly. ﴿They will say, "Alas for us over what we neglected concerning it,"﴾ we fell short and wasted the work of the Hereafter in this world. ﴿While they carry their burdens upon their backs,﴾ their loads, meaning their sins. ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they carry.﴾ What a burden they have carried.

And that is because when the disbeliever comes out of his grave, his deed meets him in the most hideous form and the foulest smell. It says: "I am your evil deed. You have ridden me for a long time in the world, so today I will ride you."

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 32:

﴿And the life of this world is nothing but amusement and diversion.﴾ Because it perishes and comes to an end, like amusement and play, a pleasure that is fleeting and will soon pass. ﴿And the Hereafter is better for those who fear God.﴾ The Hereafter is the Garden. ﴿For those who are mindful (yattaqun)﴾ of shirk. ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾ [to see] that this is so, so do not slacken in working for it. Then he consoled his Prophet (ﷺ) over the denial of him by the Quraysh, and said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 33:

﴿We indeed know that what they say grieves you﴾, openly: that you are a liar and a fabricator. ﴿Yet they do not deny you﴾ in secret, for they already knew your truthfulness. ﴿But it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of God﴾ with the Qur'an after knowing it. It was revealed concerning the obstinate who refused to submit to the truth, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them﴾ (27:14). The verse.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 34:

﴿And indeed messengers were denied before you, but they endured patiently what they were denied﴾, (seeking) my reward. ﴿And they were harmed﴾, until they were sawn apart with saws and burned with fire. ﴿Until Our help came to them﴾, meaning Our assistance to them by destroying those who denied them. ﴿And none can alter the words of Allah﴾, meaning none can overturn His judgment. He has decreed the victory of the prophets in His saying: ﴿Allah has decreed: "Surely I and My messengers will prevail"﴾. ﴿And there has already come to you some of the news of the messengers﴾, that is, their news in the Qur'an: how We saved them and destroyed their people.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 35:

﴿And if their turning away is heavy upon you﴾: it becomes great and weighs heavily. Their turning away is from belief in you and in the Qur'an. The reason is that the Prophet (ﷺ) was eager for the faith of his people, so whenever they asked him for a sign, he loved to show it to them, hoping for their belief. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿So if you are able to seek a tunnel﴾ to seek out a passage (sarab) ﴿in the earth, or a ladder﴾ a means of ascent ﴿to the sky, and bring them a sign﴾ then do so. The meaning is: you are a human being who cannot bring the signs, so there is no way for you except patience until Allah judges. ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance﴾. That is: they abandoned faith only because of My prior decree concerning them; if I had willed, they would have all gathered upon faith. ﴿So do not be among the ignorant﴾ regarding the fact that some of them will believe in you and not others, and that they will not all gather upon guidance. He made the answer severe as a rebuke to them for this state.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 36:

﴿Only those who listen will respond﴾, meaning: those who answer you to faith. ﴿Those who listen﴾ are the believers who listen to the reminder, accept it and benefit from it. As for the disbeliever, whom God has sealed upon his hearing, how will he lend an ear to the truth? ﴿And the dead﴾, meaning: the disbelievers of Mecca, ﴿God will raise them up; then to Him they will be returned﴾, that is, they will be brought back, and He will recompense them for their deeds.

They said: the chiefs of Quraysh. ﴿Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?﴾ That is, "Why would he not be sent" (lawla: "why not, would that"), meaning: the descent of an angel to bear witness to his prophethood. ﴿Say: Indeed, Allah is able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know﴾ what trial would befall them because of it, which is what we mentioned in His words: ﴿And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 38:

﴿And there is no creature on the earth, nor a bird that flies with its two wings﴾ meaning: all animals, for they are not free of these two conditions. ﴿but they are communities like you.﴾ They are classified kinds, known by their names. Every class of beasts is a community, such as birds, gazelles, flies and lions, and every kind of animal is a community, just as the children of Adam are called mankind (al-Ins). ﴿We have not neglected anything in the Book.﴾ We have not left out of the Book anything that the servants need, except that We have explained it, either explicitly (nassan), or by indication (dalalah), or in summary (mujmal), or in detail (mufassal), as in His saying: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things﴾, meaning: of everything that is needed in matters of religion. ﴿Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾, meaning: these communities will be gathered ﴿for reckoning and recompense.﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 39:

﴿And those who denied Our signs﴾ — that which Muhammad (ﷺ) brought — ﴿are deaf﴾ to the Qur'an, not hearing it with the hearing of benefit, ﴿and dumb﴾ concerning the Qur'an, not speaking it. Then He informed that they became like this by His will, so He said: ﴿Whomever Allah wills, He leaves him astray, and whomever He wills, He places him upon a straight path.﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 40:

﴿Say﴾: O Muhammad, to these polytheists who associate others with God, ﴿Tell me﴾: meaning, inform me. ﴿If there comes upon you the punishment of God﴾: he means death. ﴿Or the Hour comes upon you﴾: the Resurrection. ﴿Would you call upon other than God?﴾: that is, would you call upon these idols and stones that you have worshipped besides God? ﴿If you are truthful﴾: this is the answer to His words ﴿Tell me﴾, because it means "inform me", as if it were said: if you are truthful, inform me whom you call upon when the calamity descends upon you.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 41:

﴿Bal﴾ i.e.: you do not call upon other than Him. ﴿Iyyahu tad'una fa-yakshifu ma tad'una ilayh﴾ i.e.: He removes the harm for which you called upon Him. ﴿In sha'a wa-tansawna﴾ and you forget and abandon ﴿ma tushrikuna﴾ [the idols] you associate with Him, so you do not call upon them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 42:

﴿And We had certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you,﴾ [and] they disbelieved in them, ﴿so We seized them with adversity﴾, which is severe poverty, ﴿and hardship﴾, which is pains and illnesses, ﴿that perhaps they would humble themselves﴾, that they might submit and become humble.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 43:

﴿Why then did they not﴾ (fa-lawla) ﴿humble themselves﴾ (tadarra'u) ﴿when Our punishment came upon them﴾ (idh jā'ahum ba'sunā)? That is, why did they not ask... [see note below] — wait, correcting the rendering to follow the text faithfully:

﴿Why then, when Our punishment came upon them, did they not humble themselves﴾ (fa-lawlā idh jā'ahum ba'sunā tadarra'ū)? "Fa-halla" means "why not," and "tadhallalū" means "they humbled themselves, submitted." The meaning is: they did not humble themselves. ﴿But their hearts became hardened﴾ (qasat qulūbuhum), so they persisted in their disbelief. ﴿And Satan made attractive to them﴾ (zayyana lahumu al-shaytān) the misguidance they were upon, so they persisted.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 44:

﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾ they abandoned what they had been admonished with. ﴿We opened to them the gates of everything﴾ of blessing and joy after the adversity they had been in. ﴿Until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them﴾ while they were in their rejoicing, so that their regret would be greater. ﴿Suddenly, and then they were despairing﴾ hopeless of every good.

﴿So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off﴾ themselves. That is, their ghābir (غابرهم), the one who lags behind at the end of the people. The meaning: they were utterly uprooted by destruction, and no survivor of them remained. ﴿And all praise is due to God, Lord of the worlds﴾ for granting victory to the messengers and destroying the wrongdoers.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 46:

﴿Say: "Have you considered, if Allah were to take away your hearing and your sight"﴾ i.e., deafen you and blind you, "﴿and seal over your hearts﴾" so that you do not recognize anything, meaning: remove these faculties from you entirely, "﴿who is a deity other than Allah who could bring them back to you?﴾" i.e., bring back to you what He has taken from you. "﴿Look how We diversify the signs﴾" We make them clear to them in the Qur'an, "﴿yet they turn away﴾" they turn aside from what has become manifest to them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 47:

﴿Say, "Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah comes upon you suddenly or openly, [by night or by day], will any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?"﴾ [Those who ascribed partners to Allah.]

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 50:

﴿Say: I do not tell you that with me are the treasuries of Allah﴾ from which He provides sustenance and gives, ﴿nor do I know the unseen﴾ so that I could inform you of the outcome of what you will come to, ﴿nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾ who witnesses of Allah's affairs what human beings do not witness. ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾, that is: I only inform you of what Allah has sent down to me. ﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ The disbelievers and the believers. ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾ That the two are not equal.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 51:

﴿And warn thereby﴾ — warn with the Qur'an — ﴿those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾. He means: the believers who fear the Day of Resurrection and the terrors within it. ﴿They will have no protector or intercessor besides Him﴾. He means: intercession only occurs by His permission, and there is no intercessor or helper for anyone on the Day of Resurrection except by the permission of God. ﴿That perhaps they may be God-conscious﴾ — that they may fear in the Hereafter and refrain from what I have forbidden them.

Verse 6:52 (al-Wahidi, al-Wajiz)

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance.﴾ It was revealed concerning the poor among the believers, when the leaders of the disbelievers said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Remove these people from you, so that we may sit with you and believe in you."

The meaning of ﴿those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾ is: they worship Allah through the prescribed prayers. ﴿Seeking His countenance﴾ means they seek the reward of Allah.

﴿You are not accountable for their reckoning at all﴾ means: [you are not accountable] for their provision. ﴿Nor are they accountable for yours at all﴾ means: [their] ... Wait, correcting this: the text reads, "﴿مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾" in the first clause, so the full rendering is:

﴿You bear no responsibility for their reckoning in anything, so that you would grow weary of them and drive them away, and they bear no responsibility for your reckoning in anything.﴾ That is: your provision is not upon them, nor their provision upon you; rather, Allah, the Provider, provides for you and for them. So leave them to draw near to you, and do not drive them away, ﴿lest you be among the wrongdoers﴾ toward them by driving them away.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 53:

﴿And thus We tested some of them by means of others﴾: We afflicted the wealthy with the poor, and the noble with the lowly. ﴿So that they say﴾: that is, the chieftains, ﴿"Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?"﴾: they denied that these (the poor and weak) had preceded them in any virtue, or had been singled out for any blessing. Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿"Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?"﴾; that is, He guides to His religion only those whom He knows will be thankful.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 54:

﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you﴾: meaning the Companions and these poor believers. ﴿Say: Peace be upon you﴾: greet them with the greeting of the Muslims. ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾: Allah has made mercy incumbent upon you, as a firm and emphatic obligation. ﴿Whoever among you does evil in ignorance﴾: he means, your sins are ignorance, not disbelief or denial, because the sinner is ignorant of the degree of punishment for his disobedience. ﴿Then repents after it﴾: returns from his sin. ﴿And makes amends﴾: corrects his deed. ﴿Then indeed He is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾

And thus (﴿وكذلك﴾): just as We have explained to you in this surah Our proofs against the polytheists, ﴿We detail﴾, that is, We make clear to you Our argument and Our evidences so that the truth becomes manifest, and so that you, O Muhammad, may know the way of the criminals (al-mujrimin) in their associating partners with God in this world, and what they come to of disgrace on the Day of Resurrection, through My informing you of it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 56:

﴿Say: "Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah."﴾ The idols they worship besides Allah.

﴿Say: "I will not follow your desires."﴾ That is: you worshipped them following desire, not following proof, so I will not follow you in your desires.

﴿Then I would have gone astray, and I would not be among the guided.﴾ If I were to do that, I would be among those who have gone astray, and I would not be among those who have taken the path of guidance.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 57:

﴿Say, "Indeed, I am upon clear evidence"﴾: certainty and a manifest matter, ﴿from my Lord﴾, not following my own desires. ﴿But you have denied it﴾, that is, denied my Lord. ﴿What I have is not what you seek to hasten﴾, meaning the punishment or the signs you proposed. Then he informed them that this is in His hands, so He said: ﴿Judgment belongs only to Allah. He relates the truth﴾, that is, He speaks the true accounts (al-qasas al-haqq). As for whoever reads ﴿yaqussu al-haqq﴾ (يقص الحق), its meaning is: He decides the true decision. ﴿And He is the best of deciders﴾, those who distinguish between truth and falsehood.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 58:

﴿Say: "If I had what you are hastening for [i.e., the punishment], the matter would have been decided between me and you."﴾ That is, if the punishment you seek to hasten were with me, I would have hastened it for you, and the matter between me and you would have been settled by the swift execution of the punishment. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿And the matter would have been decided between me and you. And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾ He is most knowing of the time of their punishment, so He delays them until its appointed time, while I do not know that. His words:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 59:

﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He.﴾ The treasuries of what is hidden from the children of Adam: provision, rain, the descent of punishment, and reward and retribution. ﴿And He knows what is on the land and in the sea.﴾ The land: the deserts (al-qafar). The sea: every town that has water. Nothing happens in them except by the knowledge of God. ﴿And not a leaf falls but He knows it.﴾ Falling, and before it falls. ﴿Nor is there a grain in the darknesses of the earth﴾ in the moist soil beneath the earth. ﴿Nor anything moist or dry﴾ the moist is what grows, and the dry is what does not grow. ﴿But it is in a clear Book.﴾ God recorded all of that in a Book before He created creation.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 60:

﴿It is He who takes your souls by night⦆ (He seizes your spirits during your sleep). ﴿And He knows what you have earned by day⦆ (what you have earned of deeds). ﴿Then He raises you up therein⦆ (He returns your spirits to you during the day), ﴿that a specified term may be fulfilled⦆ (meaning: the term of life until death; that is, that you may complete your appointed lifespans).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 61:

﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants﴾. This has passed. ﴿And He sends over you guardians﴾ from among the angels, who count your deeds. ﴿Until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him in death﴾, the assistants of the Angel of Death. ﴿And they do not fail﴾ — they do not fall short and they do not neglect.

Then they are returned (ثم ردوا) — meaning: the servants are returned through death — (إلى الله مولاهم الحق) to God, their true Lord, (ألا له الحكم) Verily, to Him belongs the judgment, that is, the decision concerning them, (وهو أسرع الحاسبين) and He is the swiftest of the reckoners, that is, the most capable of recompensing.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 63:

﴿Say: "Who rescues you from the darknesses of land and sea?"﴾ This is a question of rebuke and affirmation, meaning: indeed Allah does that. ﴿From the darknesses of land and sea﴾ — their terrors and hardships. ﴿You call upon Him humbly and secretly﴾ — openly and privately. ﴿"If He rescues us from this,"﴾ meaning: from these hardships, ﴿"we will surely be among the thankful."﴾ — among the believing, obedient ones. The Quraysh used to travel by land and sea, and when they lost their way and feared destruction, they called upon Allah sincerely, and He rescued them. This is His saying:

Say: "It is Allah who delivers you from it." The verse informs that Allah, whom they called upon, is the One who delivers them, and then they associate with Him the idols, which they know to be of their own making and which neither harm nor benefit. The distress (al-karb) is the greatest of griefs. Then He informed that He is able to punish them, so He said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 65:

﴿Say, "He is the One able to send upon you punishment from above you,"﴾ such as the cry (al-sayha), the stones and the water; ﴿or from beneath your feet,﴾ such as the earth-sinking (al-khasf) and the earthquake (al-zalzala); ﴿or to confound you in factions,﴾ i.e., to mix you into sects by spreading among you divergent desires, so that you oppose one another and fight; and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿and make some of you taste the violence of others.﴾ ﴿See how We vary the signs﴾ — i.e., We explain them to them ﴿in the Qur'an﴾ — ﴿that they may understand﴾, i.e., so that they may come to know.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 66:

﴿Wa-kadhdhaba bihi﴾ (And your people denied it), that is, the Qur'an, ﴿qawmuka wa-huwa al-haqq﴾ [﴿your people denied it, though it is the truth﴾]. ﴿Qul lastu ʿalaykum bi-wakil﴾ (Say: "I am not a guardian over you"), meaning: one who has authority over you. That is, I only call you to God, and I have not been commanded to fight you or to compel you to believe. And this ruling has been abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of fighting (ayat al-qital).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 67:

﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾ For every report that God gives, there is a time and a place where it will occur without fail. ﴿And you will come to know﴾ what of it was in this world, so you will recognize it, and what of it was in the Hereafter, which will become apparent to you. He means: the punishment that they were being threatened with in this world and in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 68:

﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses﴾ with denial and mockery, ﴿then turn away from them﴾. Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger, peace be upon him, saying: "When you see the polytheists denying the Qur'an and you, and mocking them, then leave off sitting with them," ﴿until they engage in talk about something other than it﴾, meaning until their discourse is about something other than the Qur'an. ﴿And if Satan should make you forget﴾, meaning if you forget and sit down, ﴿then do not sit after the reminder﴾, so rise up when you remember. The Muslims said: "If whenever the polytheists mock the Qur'an and engage in vain talk about it we were to rise and leave them, we would not be able to sit in the Masjid al-Haram or circumambulate the House." So He permitted the believers to sit with them in order to remind them, and He said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 69:

﴿And upon those who are righteous (yattaqun)﴾ from shirk and the major sins, ﴿there is no reckoning (hisab) of theirs﴾ for their sins ﴿of anything; but it is a reminder﴾. He says: remind them with the Qur'an and with Muhammad (ﷺ), and so He permitted them to sit (qu'ud) on condition of reminding and admonishing, ﴿so that perhaps they may be righteous (yattaqun)﴾, so that righteousness may be hoped for from them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 70:

﴿Leave alone those who have taken their religion as amusement and diversion.﴾ That is: the disbelievers who, when they hear the signs of God, mock them and play around when they are mentioned. ﴿And remind [them] thereby.﴾ Admonish with the Qur'an. ﴿Lest a soul be delivered to destruction for what it has earned.﴾ Delivered to ruin and confined in Jahannam, so that it cannot find a way of escape. The meaning of the verse: remind them with the Qur'an, lest souls be handed over to destruction by their crimes, so that perhaps they will fear and be mindful [of God]. ﴿Though it offer every ransom.﴾ That is: the soul that is delivered to destruction, though it offer every ransom, that is, though it ransom itself with the world and all that is in it. ﴿Will not be accepted from it. Those are the ones who were delivered to destruction for what they earned.﴾ Handed over to ruin. ﴿For them is a drink of boiling water.﴾ Which is hot water.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 71:

﴿Say, "Shall we call upon, instead of Allah, that which can neither benefit us nor harm us?﴾ Shall we worship what possesses no power to benefit us or harm us, because it is inanimate matter? ﴿And be turned back on our heels after Allah has guided us﴾ shall we return behind us to associating partners with Allah, so that our condition becomes like that of ﴿one whom the devils have enticed in the earth﴾ — seduced and enticed by the ghouls into bewilderment — ﴿bewildered﴾, wavering, unable to find the right path ﴿who has companions calling him to guidance, "Come to us."﴾ This is the parable of one who strayed after guidance: he responds to the devil who has lured him into the desert, so he ends up in a wasteland of the earth where he perishes and disobeys the one who calls him to the right path. Likewise is one who strays after guidance. ﴿Say, "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] guidance."﴾ This is a rebuttal to those who called to the worship of idols; that is: we will not do that, because the guidance of Allah is the guidance, not any other guidance.

And He it is who created the heavens and the earth in truth. That is, with the perfection of His power, the comprehensiveness of His knowledge, and the excellence of His craftsmanship, and all of that is truth. ﴿And the day He says, "Be," and it is﴾ — mention, O Muhammad, the day He says to a thing, "Be," and it is. He means: on the Day of Resurrection He will say to the creation, "Disperse," and they will disperse.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 75:

﴿And thus did We show Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾: that is, just as We made Abraham see the repugnance of what his father was upon, the worship of idols, We showed him ﴿the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾. It means their sovereignty: the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees and the seas. Allah the Exalted showed him these things until he looked at them, taking heed and taking them as evidence for their Creator. As for His saying ﴿and that he might be among the certain (al-muqinin)﴾, it is a conjunction on the meaning; its implied sense is: so that he might draw evidence from them, and so that he might be among the certain.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 76:

﴿When the night covered him﴾, i.e., concealed him and grew dark, ﴿he saw a star and said: "This is my lord"﴾, i.e., according to your claim, O you who speak of the judgment of the stars. That is because they were people of the stars, who saw in them the governance of creation. ﴿Then when it set﴾, i.e., disappeared, ﴿he said: "I do not love those that set."﴾ He made them aware of their ignorance and error in exalting the stars, and he indicated that whoever disappears after appearing is created and subjugated, and is not a lord.

﴿Falamma ra'a al-qamara bazighan﴾ (When he saw the moon rising), meaning appearing, so he argued against them concerning the moon and the sun with the same argument he had used against them concerning the star. His saying: ﴿La'in lam yahdini Rabbi﴾ (Unless my Lord guides me), meaning: unless He keeps me firm upon guidance. And his saying to the sun:

﴿This is my Lord﴾. He did not say "this one" (hadhihi) because the word "sun" (al-shams) is masculine in grammatical gender, and because "sun" here means light and radiance, so the speech was construed according to the meaning. ﴿This is greater﴾, that is, greater than the star and the moon. When the proof was established against his people, he said: ﴿Indeed, I am free from what you associate (with Allah)﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 79:

﴿Indeed, I have turned my face﴾ meaning: I have made my intention, in my worship and my affirmation of the oneness of God, Mighty and Majestic, toward Him. The rest of the verse has been explained earlier.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 80:

﴿And his people argued with him⦆ they disputed with him and contended with him over his abandoning of their gods and his worship of God, and they frightened him that their gods would afflict him with harm. So he said: ﴿Do you argue with me concerning God?﴾ That is: concerning His worship and His oneness. ﴿When He has guided me﴾ He has made clear to me that by which I was guided. ﴿And I do not fear what you associate with Him﴾ of idols, that they might afflict me with harm, ﴿except that my Lord should will something.﴾ Indeed I fear nothing except the will of God, that He might punish me. ﴿My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge﴾ He knows them with complete knowledge. ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ That is: will you not take heed and abandon the worship of idols?

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 81:

﴿How should I fear what you have associated (with Allah)?﴾ That is, the idols. He denies that he should fear them. ﴿Yet you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has sent down to you no authority.﴾ That is, for which you have no proof or evidence for associating it with Allah. ﴿So which of the two parties has more right to security?﴾ That is, which of them is more entitled to be safe from punishment: the monotheist or the polytheist?

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 82:

﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾ — they do not mingle their faith with shirk (associating partners with God). ﴿For them there is security﴾ from the punishment, ﴿and they are the guided﴾ to the religion of God.

This is the commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 83:

﴿And that was Our argument⦆ — meaning: the argument with which he argued against them. ﴿We gave it to Abraham⦆ — We inspired Abraham and guided him to it. ﴿We raise in degrees whom We will⦆ — their ranks, through knowledge and understanding. Then he mentioned Noah and those among the prophets, from among his descendants, whom He guided, up to His words:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 86:

﴿And all﴾: that is, of those mentioned here. ﴿We preferred over the worlds﴾: over the people of their times.

"And [We guided] some of their fathers" — ﴿ومن آبائهم﴾ means: and We guided some of their fathers, ﴿and their descendants and their brothers﴾. Here "min" (from) is for partiality (tab'id), meaning "some of."

﴿That is the guidance of God﴾: the religion of God that they follow.
﴿He guides thereby whomever He wills﴾: meaning, He guides to it whomever He wills
﴿of His servants﴾.
﴿And if they had associated [others with Him]﴾: worshipped other than Me.
﴿Their deeds would have been nullified﴾: became void.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 89:

﴿Those are the ones to whom We gave the Book﴾ meaning: the scriptures that He sent down to them, ﴿and the judgment﴾ meaning: the knowledge and understanding. ﴿So if these [people] disbelieve in them﴾ i.e., in Our signs, ﴿these﴾ the people of Makkah, ﴿then We have entrusted with them﴾ i.e., We have appointed for them ﴿a people﴾ whom We have granted success in them, and they are the Muhajirun (the Emigrants) and the Ansar (the Helpers).

ُ﴿Those are the ones whom God guided﴾, meaning: the prophets who were mentioned earlier. ﴿So follow their guidance﴾, that is: be patient as they were patient, for their people denied them and they persevered. ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any wage for it﴾, that is, for the Qur'an and the conveying of the message, ﴿a wage﴾, meaning wealth that you would give me. ﴿It is not but a reminder to the worlds﴾, meaning: the Qur'an is nothing but an admonition to all creatures.

﴿They did not measure God with His true measure﴾: they did not magnify God with His due magnification, and they did not describe Him with His true description. ﴿When they said, "God has not sent down anything to any human."﴾ This was because the Jews denied that God, Mighty and Majestic, had sent down a Book from heaven, thereby denying the Qur'an. ﴿Say﴾ to them, O Muhammad: ﴿"Who sent down the Book that Moses brought?"﴾ meaning: the Torah. ﴿"You make it into scrolls"﴾ written down, and you deposit it in them. ﴿"You disclose them"﴾ meaning the scrolls: they disclose what they like and conceal the description of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿"And you were taught what neither you nor your fathers knew"﴾ in the Torah, but you wasted it and did not benefit from it. ﴿Say, "God."﴾ That is, God sent it down. ﴿Then leave them in their plunging﴾: their falsehood, their vain talk, ﴿playing﴾, doing what brings them no benefit.

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on Surah 6, verse 92:**

﴿And this is a Book﴾, meaning: the Qur'an, ﴿which We have sent down, blessed﴾, its good abundant and its benefit lasting, giving glad tidings of reward and warning against what is ugly, along with countless other blessings. ﴿Confirming what came before it﴾, in agreement with the earlier Books. ﴿That you may warn the Mother of Cities﴾, meaning the people of Makkah, ﴿and those around it﴾, meaning the people of all the other regions. ﴿Those who believe in the Hereafter﴾, with a true belief, ﴿believe in it﴾, in the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 93:

﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah﴾. It was revealed concerning Musaylima and al-Aswad al-Ansi, who both claimed prophethood and that Allah had revealed to them. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿or says, "It has been revealed to me," while nothing has been revealed to him, and [who] says, "I will reveal the like of what Allah has revealed"﴾. It means: the mockers who said: ﴿If we willed, we could say the like of this﴾. ﴿And if you could see﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿when the wrongdoers are﴾, meaning those mentioned, ﴿in the agonies of death﴾, its severe trials and terrors, ﴿while the angels extend their hands﴾ toward them with striking and torment, ﴿[saying], "Discharge your souls"﴾. That is, they say this, and the soul of the disbeliever departs with hardship and reluctance, because it is going toward the most severe punishment, and the angels compel them to release the spirit, saying: ﴿Discharge your souls﴾ unwillingly. ﴿Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation﴾, that is, the punishment in which severe disgrace befalls them, ﴿for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth﴾, namely that revelation had come to you when it had not, ﴿and you were arrogant toward His verses﴾, exalting yourselves against believing in them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 94:

﴿And indeed you have come to Us alone, as We created you the first time.﴾ It is said to the disbelievers in the Hereafter: "You have come to Us alone, without family, without wealth, and without anything you had put forward," ﴿as We created you the first time﴾, as you came out of the wombs of your mothers. ﴿And you have left behind what We bestowed upon you﴾, that is, what We made you possess and gave you of wealth, slaves, and livestock, ﴿behind your backs. And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed to be partners [with Allah] among you.﴾ This is because the polytheists used to worship idols, claiming that they were Allah's partners and that they were their intercessors with Him. ﴿Now your bonds have been severed﴾, meaning your connection and affection, ﴿and what you used to claim has vanished from you﴾, meaning what you used to claim [to be true] and used to deny in the world, has gone from you.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 95:

﴿Indeed, Allah is the Splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾, splitting them for vegetation. ﴿He brings the living out of the dead﴾, bringing forth the sperm-drop as a living human being. ﴿And brings the dead out of the living﴾, the sperm-drop from the living. And it is said: He brings the believer out of the disbeliever and the disbeliever out of the believer. ﴿That is Allah﴾, who did these things that you witness, ﴿your Lord﴾. ﴿So how are you deluded?﴾ From where are you turned away from the truth after the clear proof!

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 96:

﴿Fāliq al-iṣbāḥ﴾ (the Cleaver of the dawn): splitting the column of the morning from the darkness and blackness of the night, in the sense that He is its Creator and Originator. ﴿And He made the night for rest﴾: for creation, who rest in it with the rest of comfort. ﴿And the sun and the moon as a reckoning﴾: and He made the sun and the moon subject to a reckoning, which they do not exceed, as they revolve in a calculated course. ﴿That is the decree of the Almighty﴾: in His dominion, He does what He wills. ﴿The All-Knowing﴾: of what He has decreed in creating them both.

Translation:

﴿It is He who produced you from a single soul﴾, meaning Adam. ﴿And for you is a place of settlement﴾, that is, for you is a settled place in the wombs. ﴿And a place of storage﴾, in the loins (aṣlāb).

﴿It is He who sends down water from the sky﴾, meaning: rain. ﴿And We brought forth thereby the growth of every thing﴾, which grows. ﴿Then We brought forth﴾ from that growth ﴿green [shoots]﴾, green like wheat, barley and maize, and whatever moist and green grain-bearing plants grow. ﴿From it We bring forth﴾ from the green [shoots] ﴿grain, piled up﴾, one part of it upon another in a single ear. ﴿And from the palm trees, from their spathe﴾, the first thing that emerges from it, ﴿are clusters﴾, meaning: the stalks that hang down from the spathe, ﴿hanging low﴾ within reach of whoever picks them, meaning: the short palm trees whose bunches reach down to the ground. ﴿And gardens﴾, meaning: We brought forth with the water gardens ﴿of grapes, and the olive﴾, and olive trees, ﴿and the pomegranate﴾, and pomegranate trees, ﴿resembling one another﴾ in colour, meaning: the pomegranates, ﴿and not resembling﴾ in taste, meaning: differing in taste. It was also said: resembling in their leaves, differing in their fruit. ﴿Look at their fruit﴾, with the gaze of inference and consideration, when it first forms, ﴿and [when] it ripens﴾, its maturing. ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe﴾, who affirm that He who brought forth this vegetation is able to give life to the dead.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 100:

﴿And they made the jinn partners with Allah﴾: they obeyed the devils in worshipping idols, so they made them partners with Allah. ﴿And they attributed to Him sons and daughters﴾: they fabricated this as a lie and an act of disbelief. He means: those who said the angels are the daughters of Allah, and the Jews and the Christians, when they claimed that Allah has a son. ﴿Without knowledge﴾: they did not mention it from knowledge; they only mentioned it as a lie.

Wahidi's commentary (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 101:

And His saying: ﴿How can He have a child when He has no consort?﴾ That is: from where could He have a child? A child is not born except from a consort, and He has no consort. ﴿And He created all things﴾ That is: and He is the Creator of all things.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 103:

﴿No visual perceptions can grasp Him﴾ in this world, because He has promised the vision in the Hereafter, by His saying: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ (75:22-23), and the absolute (muṭlaq) is to be understood in terms of the restricted (muqayyad). It was also said: visual perceptions do not encompass His essence (kunh) and reality (ḥaqīqah), yet they do see Him; so visual perceptions see the Creator but do not encompass Him. ﴿And He perceives the visual perceptions﴾: He sees them and encompasses them with knowledge, unlike created beings, who do not grasp the reality of sight, nor the thing by which a human sees through his eyes rather than through other organs. ﴿And He is the Subtle (al-Laṭīf)﴾: the Gentle toward His allies. ﴿the All-Aware (al-Khabīr)﴾ of them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 104:

﴿Indeed there has come to you insight (baṣā'ir) from your Lord.﴾ He means: the clear proofs of the Qur'an. ﴿So whoever sees clearly﴾ is guided, ﴿it is for his own self that he has acted﴾. ﴿And whoever is blind, it is against himself﴾ that he has committed the punishment; he has brought the torment upon his own self. ﴿And I am not a guardian over you﴾ — a watcher over your deeds — ﴿so that I would recompense you for them.﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 105:

﴿And thus﴾ just as We have made clear in this surah, ﴿We vary﴾ We explain ﴿the signs﴾ in the Qur'an, calling them by them and warning them, ﴿and [so] that they may say, "You have studied [it]"﴾ a conjunction with the implicit pronoun in meaning; the sense and the estimation: We vary the signs so that the proof is binding upon them, and that they may say, "You have studied," i.e., "You have learned it from Yasar, Jabr and the Jews." The meaning of "studied" (darasa) is: he recited it under the guidance of another. The meaning of this lam in His words ﴿and that they may say﴾ is the meaning of lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah), i.e., We vary the signs so that the final outcome of their affair becomes a denial, due to the wretchedness that overtook them. ﴿And We make it clear to a people who know﴾ meaning: His friends whom He guided, and those who were made happy by the clarification of the truth.

[Qur'an 6:107] "And if God had willed, they would not have associated others with Him." That is: if God had willed, He would have made them believers. "And We did not make you a guardian over them." You were not sent to protect the polytheists from punishment; you were sent only as a conveyer of the message. So do not grieve over their polytheism, for that is by the will of God.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 108:

﴿And do not revile those whom they call upon besides Allah﴾ meaning: their idols and objects of worship. Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 136:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 138:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 148:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 152:

﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best, until he reaches his maturity (ashuddah).﴾ That is: to improve his property, to manage it in a way that makes it grow, and then to eat from it in a reasonable manner if he is in need of it. ﴿Until he reaches his maturity.﴾ That is: preserve it for him until he has reached puberty (ihtilam). ﴿And give full measure and weight.﴾ That is: complete them without any deficiency. ﴿And the scale.﴾ That is: the weight of the scale. ﴿With justice.﴾ That is: with fairness, neither diminishing nor exceeding. ﴿We do not charge any soul except within its capacity.﴾ That is: only what it can bear and what does not strain it. And this means that if the one giving were charged with giving extra, his soul would be strained by it; likewise, if the one receiving were charged with taking less. ﴿And when you speak, be just, even if it concerns a near relative.﴾ That is: when you testify or speak, say the truth, ﴿even if﴾ the one it is in favor of or against ﴿is a relative.﴾

And that this is My path, straight, so follow it. And do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way. That is what He has enjoined upon you, that you may be mindful of Him.

Translation of the passage, following the given instructions:

﴿وأنّ هذا﴾ And [it is] because this (is so): ﴿صراطي مستقيماً﴾ — meaning: My religion is the religion of the ḥanafiyya (the upright monotheistic faith), the most upright of religions. ﴿فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل﴾ — "follow it, and do not follow the ways," namely Judaism (al-Yahudiyya), Christianity (al-Nasraniyya), Zoroastrianism (al-Majusiyya), and the worship of idols. ﴿فتفرَّق بكم عن سبيله﴾ — "lest they scatter you away from His way," i.e., lead you astray from His religion. ﴿ذلكم﴾ — that which was mentioned — ﴿وصَّاكم﴾ — "He has enjoined you," i.e., commanded you to it in the Book — ﴿لعلكم تتقون﴾ — "so that you may be mindful," i.e., that you may guard yourselves against the ways.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 154:

﴿Thumma ātaynā﴾ means: then I inform you that We gave ﴿Musa the Book, completely, upon the one who did good﴾, meaning: upon the one whom Musa perfected in knowledge, wisdom and the earlier books of God, i.e. he knew them. The meaning of ﴿tamaman﴾ (completely) upon that is: in addition to it, until knowledge of what We had given him was complete for him. ﴿Wa-tafsīlan﴾ (and detailed explanation) means: We gave it for completeness and detailed explanation, and tafsīl is clarification. ﴿La'allahum bi-liqā'i rabbihim yu'minūn﴾ means: so that they would believe in the resurrection and affirm the reward and punishment.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 155:

﴿And this is a Book﴾, meaning: the Qur'an, ﴿which We have sent down, blessed﴾. Its explanation has already passed in this surah.

﴿An taqulu﴾ — lest you say: ﴿"The Book was only sent down to two groups before us"﴾, meaning the Jews and the Christians, ﴿"and we were indeed unaware of their study."﴾ And we were only unaware of reciting their books. The address is to the people of Makkah, and the purpose is to establish the proof against them by the sending down of the Qur'an upon Muhammad (ﷺ), so that they would not say on the Day of Resurrection: "The Torah and the Gospel were sent down to two groups before us, and we were unaware of what was in them."

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 157:

And His words: ﴿وَصَدَفَ عَنْهَا﴾ (and turned away from them), meaning: he turned aside.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 158:

﴿Are they waiting﴾ for you, when they deny you, ﴿except that the angels should come to them﴾ at death, to take their souls. We have explained the meaning of ﴿waiting﴾ in Surat al-Baqarah. ﴿Or that your Lord should come﴾, that is, His command concerning them to kill them. ﴿Or that some of the signs of your Lord should come﴾, meaning: the rising of the sun from its west. The meaning is: these who denied you will either die and fall into punishment, or the sword will be commanded against them, or they will be given respite for the duration of the world, so that they multiply and enjoy its pleasures. Then, when the signs of the Resurrection appear, ﴿faith will not benefit a soul that did not believe before, or that had not earned good through its faith﴾, meaning, that had not previously performed an act of obedience while being a believer. ﴿Say: Wait﴾ for one of these things, ﴿indeed we are waiting﴾ for one of them concerning you.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 159:

﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion﴾ means: the Jews and the Christians, who took up some of what they were commanded and abandoned some of it, like His saying, reporting about them: ﴿Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part?﴾ ﴿And they became sects﴾, that is, divided factions, some of whom declare others to be disbelievers. ﴿You have nothing to do with them in anything﴾ means: you were not commanded to fight them. Then, when he was commanded to fight them, this was abrogated (naskh).

ſ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed﴾ — whoever among the believers does a good deed — ﴿will have ten times its like﴾ — ten good deeds are recorded for him. ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed﴾ — a sin — ﴿will not be recompensed except with its like﴾ — that is, the recompense will be equal to it and not more than it. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ — the reward of their deeds will not be diminished.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 161:

﴿Say, "Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a correct religion"﴾. That is: He made known to me a religion ﴿qayyiman﴾, upright and straight.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 162:

﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer and my rites of sacrifice﴾ (my worship, from my pilgrimage and my sacrifice) ﴿and my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ That is: it is He who gives me life and it is He who causes me to die, and I direct my prayer and all the rites of worship to Allah, not to anyone else.
and His saying: ﴿And of that I have been commanded﴾ — that is, it has been revealed to me ﴿and I am the first of the Muslims﴾ — of this nation.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 6, verse 164:

﴿Say: Shall I seek a lord other than Allah?﴾ (a lord): a master and a deity. ﴿while He is the Lord of all things﴾: their Owner and Master. ﴿And no soul earns [blame] except against itself﴾: no soul commits a sin except that it is held accountable for it. ﴿And no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another﴾. He means: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah used to say: "Follow my way and I will bear your sins," so Allah revealed: ﴿And no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another﴾, meaning no one bears the crime of another, so that the wrongdoer is not held accountable for it.

And He it is Who made you successors (khala'if) of the earlier nations upon the earth, by destroying them and making you inheritors of the earth after them. And He raised some of you above others in degrees, through wealth and provision, that He may test you in what He has given you. Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment toward His enemies, and indeed He is Forgiving toward His friends, Merciful to them.
